[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant provided a timeline of the Internet and World Wide Web development, including key events:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1960s: Introduction of packet switching and computer networking.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1969: Creation of ARPANET by the US Department of Defense.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1972: Invention of email by Ray Tomlinson.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1983: Introduction of the Domain Name System (DNS).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1989: Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web and the first web browser, WorldWideWeb.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1991: Creation of the first web page.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1993: Release of the first popular web browser, Mosaic.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1995: Commercialization of the Internet began with online shopping sites like Amazon and eBay.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1998: Launch of Google.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2004: Launch of Facebook.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2007: Release of the first iPhone.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2016: Popularization of the Internet of Things (IoT).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Important figures in the development of the Internet and World Wide Web include Vince Cerf, Bob Kahn, Tim Berners-Lee, Marc Andreessen, Larry Page, Sergey Brin, Mark Zuckerberg, and Elon Musk.
